prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1453; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at the signal on the northbound approach of a Pearland, Texas intersection when the vehicle behind them, identified as Driver 2, made contact with the rear bumper. Driver 1 reported neck and lower back discomfort at the scene and stated that a passenger was seated in the rear of the vehicle at the time of impact. The passenger's exact seating position could not be firmly established from the statements taken, and it remains unclear whether the reported back strain resulted from this collision or from another cause. Scene photographs confirm the general point of impact and the position of both vehicles, but no independent witnesses came forward. Some of the damage visible on the rear of Driver 1's vehicle may pre-date this event, and the extent attributable to this impact has not been determined. Driver 1 advised that the vehicle had no prior damage known to them. Driver 2 is not listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle and does not reside with the policyholder. Further review is recommended before any conclusions are drawn regarding causation or injury.
